data.narrative: Learner demonstrated mastery of reproduction science and concurrency debugging throughout Module 03. Rather than guessing at intermittent 500 errors on popular links, the student engineered a minimal concurrent reproduction script that forced the check-then-act database collision (Bug #5) to trigger deterministically (9/10 crashes). Furthermore, in the break step, the student caught insidious silent data corruption (out-of-order timestamp clobbering) and enforced monotonic atomic upserts to guarantee exact counts and consistent access clocks.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected Synthetic Reproduction (Option B) with sharp engineering rationale, recognizing that synthetic test harnesses isolate concurrency variables in minutes without the security/PII liabilities of production replay.
dimension_scores.evidence: Argued that synthetic scripts produce shareable, portable CI regression tests while production captures introduce background noise and compliance hazards.

dimension_scores.observation: Systematically eliminated data shape and timing boundary hypotheses, isolating concurrency as the sole trigger using a 10-request concurrent Promise.all harness.
dimension_scores.evidence: Demonstrated that serial requests succeed 100% of the time, while concurrent check-then-act execution crashes with unique constraint collisions.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized how unhandled race conditions and unique constraint collisions can be weaponized for denial of service on high-traffic endpoints.
dimension_scores.evidence: Enforced atomic database-level constraints and upsert locks to prevent concurrent request starvation.

dimension_scores.observation: Distinguished clearly between loud failures (HTTP 500 crashes) and silent data corruption (out-of-order timestamp overwrites), solving both at the storage layer.
dimension_scores.evidence: Implemented monotonic timestamp guards (GREATEST / targetTimestamp logic) so delayed earlier requests cannot roll back the clock on newer accesses.

dimension_scores.observation: Documented the entire scientific investigation in progress/module-03-diagnosis.md with pristine reproduction logs, SQL breakdowns, and verification matrices.
dimension_scores.evidence: Explained the check-then-act mechanism clearly using thread interleaving timelines and database lock serialization.

strengths: Ability to convert intermittent 'flaky' production incidents into deterministic, reproducible test scripts
Vigilance regarding silent data corruption: refused to declare victory just because HTTP error rates dropped to zero
growth_areas: Apply this performance and concurrency mindset to profiling tools and query latency bottlenecks in Module 04
data.recommendation: Advance to Module 04 (The Debugging Toolbox) to master profilers and identify silent N+1 query loops.

public_evidence.student_action: Engineered minimal concurrent reproduction harness and fixed check-then-act race collisions and silent timestamp overwrites with atomic database upserts
public_evidence.technical_detail: Replaced non-atomic findUnique/create with Prisma upsert on @@unique([linkId, timestampBucket]) and monotonic lastAccessedAt guard
public_evidence.proof: verify-module-03-debug.ts passed 100%: reproduced 9 crashes under check-then-act, achieved 10/10 successes with exact count=10 on atomic upsert, and preserved monotonic timestamps
public_evidence.ability: Reproduces and eliminates non-deterministic concurrency bugs and silent data corruption using atomic database primitives
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows candidate does not write off production anomalies as 'flaky' and can design robust concurrent data pipelines that eliminate race conditions
